target: A release has 20 independent anomaly monitors. During one decision window, any monitor may trigger a rollback. The team wants the family-wise probability of at least one false rollback under the global null to be 5%, and must set one equal per-monitor p-value threshold. A raw 0.05 threshold on each monitor is not acceptable.
surface: A previous observability setup gave every one of 20 monitors a p-value threshold of 0.05, treating each alarm independently and not controlling the probability that at least one false rollback occurs across the family.
structural: An industrial sensor study used the Sidak correction for m independent tests. To achieve family-wise error alpha with one equal local threshold, it set alpha_local=1-(1-alpha)^(1/m), so that 1-(1-alpha_local)^m=alpha.
rubric: Explicitly selects the Sidak independent-tests family-wise correction rather than raw 0.05 or only qualitative caution.
Recommends each monitor use p<=about 0.00256 and explains this yields 5% family-wise error.
States the independence assumption and distinguishes Sidak from the conservative Bonferroni approximation 0.0025.
